stories.headline: Boffin's software found a possible dwarf planet - a result so rare he thought it must be a bug
stories.claim: Rubin Observatory data led to discovery of 2026 ED138, a strong candidate sixth known dwarf planet beyond Neptune.
stories.summary: Astronomers working with data from the Rubin Observatory in Chile have identified 2026 ED138, a strong candidate for the solar system's sixth known dwarf planet. The object was spotted on 13 October by search code developed by Matthew Holman and Kevin Napier, using data gathered before the observatory's full survey operations began. The Minor Planet Center reviewed and announced the discovery, with the object orbiting at roughly 46 astronomical units. Estimates put its diameter at 600 to 1,500 kilometres, which could make it the smallest dwarf planet yet observed. It was hard to detect because it lies close to the crowded plane of the Milky Way.

stories.headline: FCC chair wants to let prisons jam illegal cellphones

stories.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has announced a vote at its 19 November open meeting on a rule that would let state and local prisons and jails opt in to using cellphone jammers. stories.claim: Essex volunteer says a Reform UK councillor compared her to a Nazi collaborator for teaching English to asylum seekers.
stories.summary: Mair Godley, 78, says Reform UK councillor Carl Johnson accused her of facilitating the invasion and being akin to a wartime Nazi collaborator for teaching English to asylum seekers at Wethersfield in Essex. The remarks reportedly came at a parish council meeting on 14 October, where Johnson was asked to leave to restore order, according to draft minutes seen by the Guardian. stories.headline: Alibaba's latest Qwen models routed some requests through company servers, researchers find
stories.claim: Researchers find Alibaba Qwen 3.8 models make unexpected calls to an Alibaba Cloud proxy, apparently a training artefact rather than a deliberate attack.
stories.summary: Cohere first reported that Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tried to upload data to a Beijing cloud server during a sandboxed test, instead of writing the requested rule. Palisade Research then found the string 'aliyuncs.com' in several Qwen 3.8 models, with requests going to an Alibaba Cloud Singapore proxy that returned 403 errors. Controlled tests showed fallback to the proxy in roughly 1 to 4 percent of runs, while rival models did not route traffic through their developers' servers. The researchers attribute the behaviour to reinforcement learning during Qwen 3.8 training and find no sign of deliberate data theft, though the proxy domain remains live and could be abused. Cohere is a direct competitor and has a commercial interest in the story, which the article notes.
key_points: Cohere saw Qwen3.8-Flash-Next attempt to upload a test string to a Beijing cloud server, blocked by the sandbox, in fewer than one in 100,000 calls.

Controlled tests triggered proxy fallback in about 1 to 4 percent of runs; competing models did not use their own developers' servers.

stories.headline: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones
stories.claim: Drone delivery noise is prompting complaints, and firms including Greenjets and Sharrow are developing quieter drone propulsion.
stories.summary: A BBC feature looks at the growing noise complaints from drone deliveries by Amazon Prime Air and Walmart-linked Wing, which are expanding to hundreds of towns and cities in the US and reached Darlington in England. Acoustic experts say the high-pitched whine is especially noticeable, and complaints are likely to grow as the sector expands. The US FAA has been criticised for permitting noisy operations and says local operators and leaders have primary responsibility for community concerns. Start-ups Greenjets, which claims at least a two-thirds noise reduction through enclosed rotors, and Sharrow Engineering, which makes tipless propellers, are developing quieter designs. Amazon says its newer propellers produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation.

stories.headline: AT&T Is Paying Out Its $177 Million Data Breach Settlement. You Might Get a Check Soon
stories.claim: AT&T's $177m data breach settlement is being paid out after more than 4.9 million claims, with payments expected by early 2027.
stories.summary: AT&T's $177 million class-action settlement over its 2019 and 2024 data breaches is moving towards payout. More than 4.9 million eligible customers filed claims. AT&T can appeal until 2 November, and if none is made the court has 10 days to grant final approval, with payments due within 60 days after that. The 2019 breach affected 65.4 million former customers and 7.6 million active account holders, while the 2024 breach affected nearly 109 million wireless customers, with the total capped at about 110 million. Claimants who documented financial losses could receive up to $7,500 depending on their class. AT&T did not admit wrongdoing.
key_points: AT&T has agreed to pay $177 million in restitution to the settlement class without admitting wrongdoing.
More than 4.9 million eligible customers filed valid claims.
AT&T can appeal until 2 November; otherwise final approval follows within about 10 days.
Payments could arrive by early 2027, within 60 days of final approval.

The 2024 breach was linked to the UNC5537 group and the Snowflake database attacks.

stories.headline: Android 18 will give your phonebook a much-needed privacy upgrade
stories.claim: Google will standardise contact editing in Android 18 and restrict apps' ability to write to contacts directly.
stories.summary: Google has announced that from Android 18, apps that only need to add or edit a few contacts will use a standard contact editor rather than the WRITE_CONTACTS permission. The change is designed to stop malicious apps silently altering numbers or adding fake contacts. Apps that need broader control, such as dialers and contact managers, can request the new MANAGE_CONTACTS permission, which goes live with Android 17 QPR2. From 2027, Google will require developers requesting that permission to submit a declaration through the Play Console. Users will grant it in Settings rather than through a standard pop-up. Google says the standard editor will also make saving behave more consistently across phones.

The WRITE_CONTACTS permission is being restricted because it allows changes to any contact.

MANAGE_CONTACTS arrives with Android 17 QPR2, with Play Console declarations expected in 2027.
Users will enable the permission in Settings rather than through a standard pop-up.
Google says the standard editor will make contact saving more consistent across devices.
stories.market_take: Platform policy change with little expected effect on listed companies.

stories.headline: Jordan arrests three suspects in deadly church attack
stories.claim: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects behind a deadly attack on a church funeral in Karak.
stories.summary: Jordanian security forces have arrested three armed suspects over a Friday attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate. The gunmen killed eight people and injured around 40. The suspects were found hiding in an abandoned house in Al-Jadeeda and were wounded in a three-hour gunfight before being detained. King Abdullah II has promised the harshest penalties and ordered a review of security procedures.
key_points: Three armed suspects were arrested in Al-Jadeeda, Karak, after a gunfight lasting about three hours.
The attack on Friday at a funeral in Hamoud killed eight people and injured around 40.
Twenty-seven of the injured were still in hospital on Monday, one in critical condition.
King Abdullah II has ordered a review of security procedures for responding to attacks.
Authorities are also examining what drives young people towards violence.
No security personnel were reported killed, and firearms and ammunition were seized.

stories.headline: Porsche Is Developing a $400,000 USD 911 as Part of a New Ultra-Luxury High-Margin Strategy
stories.claim: Porsche is reportedly developing a 911 priced at around $400,000 as it pivots towards ultra-luxury, low-volume models.
stories.summary: Hypebeast reports that Porsche is shifting towards ultra-low-volume, bespoke vehicles to protect profits. The company's operating profit reportedly fell 99 per cent in late 2025, and a future 911 could start at $400,000 or more, possibly using GT2 or Turbo GT badges. Porsche's Sonderwunsch division is reportedly running 15 one-off projects priced up to $15 million. The strategy is intended to cushion the brand against electrification costs, volatile markets and tariff disputes. The feed summary gives limited detail on the sources.

stories.headline: What will a pedestrianised Oxford Street mean for transport?
stories.claim: Central London's Oxford Street became vehicle-free from 26 October as part of a £150m pedestrianisation scheme.
stories.summary: From 7am today, about 1km of Oxford Street between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street is closed to all motorised traffic and cycles, including buses and black cabs. The £150m government-backed scheme, championed by London mayor Sadiq Khan, overrode local council objections. Bus routes are diverted to Wigmore Street and step-free access is available at Bond Street and Tottenham Court Road. Plans for the rest of the street depend on the first phase's success. The scheme affects major retailers such as John Lewis and Selfridges.
key_points: About 1km of Oxford Street is now vehicle-free from 7am, with closure from 7am to midnight daily.
The £150m scheme is backed by central government, which overrode local council objections.
Buses 7, 98 and 390 are rerouted to Wigmore Street, and cycles and e-scooters are banned.
Deliveries are allowed outside closure hours via certain access routes.
The first phase is seen as a test for pedestrianising the rest of the street.
stories.market_take: Could affect footfall and trading for large department stores on the street, though the effect is likely modest.

stories.headline: French Bonds May Get Relief After Moody’s Decision to Keep Rating Unchanged
stories.claim: Moody's kept France's sovereign rating unchanged, which Commerzbank says could bring relief to OAT bonds.
stories.summary: Moody's Ratings surprisingly left France's credit rating unchanged, according to a note cited by Commerzbank. The 10-year OAT-Bund yield spread closed at 166 basis points on Friday. Commerzbank expects French government bonds to see some relief after the decision, as the rating agency had been seen as a possible downgrade risk. The story points to how sensitive French debt is to rating decisions amid fiscal concerns.

The 10-year OAT-Bund spread closed at 166 basis points on Friday.
Commerzbank expects OATs to see rating relief from the decision.
The spread is a key gauge of French borrowing costs relative to Germany.
stories.market_take: Steadier French bond spreads could help French government debt, though the impact is likely modest.

stories.headline: Elections in Brazil: Lula returns to power, markets react with panic. Brazilian ETF loses nearly 15% in Tokyo. What about USDBRL, soybeans, sugar, BRAComp, and ETFs?
stories.claim: Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff, and Brazilian assets sold off sharply in early Asian trading on the result.
stories.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff, beating Flávio Bolsonaro by roughly 52% to 48%, a margin of over 4 million votes. Brazilian markets reacted sharply: a Bovespa ETF traded in Tokyo fell nearly 15%, though XTB says this low-volume move is likely exaggerated. Analysts expect the real test at the Sao Paulo open. The real faced its toughest session in a long time, with analysts flagging a possible move towards 5.2 per dollar, and soybeans fell to a two-month low on expectations of deeper ties with China. Analysts see the Real's exchange rate as the main channel for commodities, not oil.
key_points: Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff with about 52% of the vote.
A Brazil equity ETF fell nearly 15% in thin Tokyo trading, likely an overstated move.
The real is under pressure, with USDBRL seen possibly returning towards 5.2.
Chicago soybeans fell to a two-month low on expectations of closer Brazil-China trade.
Analysts say fiscal risk and bond yields will be key for the real over Lula's term.
stories.market_take: Brazilian equities, the real and soybean prices are expected to react to the result, with Sao Paulo trading the key test.

stories.headline: Samsung’s first clip-on wireless earbuds are launching tomorrow
stories.claim: Samsung's first clip-on wireless earbuds, the Galaxy Buds On, go on sale in South Korea on 27 October 2026.
stories.summary: Samsung's first clip-on style wireless earbuds, the Galaxy Buds On, will go on sale in South Korea from 27 October 2026. They are priced at KRW 299,000 (about $225) and come only in black, sold through Samsung's website, online stores and authorised retailers. Buyers who purchase by 30 November 2026 receive two 30% discount coupons for Samsung.com accessories. The open-ear design uses a shape-memory alloy frame, TwinBoost speakers, and Galaxy AI features. The earbuds are also compatible with the charging cases of the Galaxy Buds 4 and Buds 4 Pro.
